abstract: We study seven rational entries subject to four regular-quintuple equations, consisting of two twin fifths and a common regular fifth over two complementary pairs. Releasing a previously imposed difference-trace relation gives a three-parameter rational chart for the pair invariants and a fully rooted base triple. A nonzero Jacobian proves that this base is three-dimensional. Four explicit scalar square equations recover the original individual entries and seventeen pairwise square roots. The classical regularity identities then give a concrete decoder from one additional root to all twenty-one, including cases with zero known spokes. We exhibit an infinite fully rooted quintuple section inside the chart. The quintuple itself is the classical nonzero regular fifth over a regular quadruple with pair product three; its simultaneous four-window embedding yields two explicit remaining gates of the form $H(t)$ and $H(-t)$, with $H$ a sextic and $t^2-12$ already square. Their product gives a genus-two necessary quotient, while the full simultaneous source cover has genus twenty-one. The supplement verifies the rational-function identities, the rational quintuple control, and fixed finite-field decoder controls using exact arithmetic. This construction does not improve the universal square cost of regular build orders and supplies no rational seventeen-root seven-set or septuple. Its contribution is a rational chart with explicit original-root lifting conditions and an inhabited source for further deformation.
author: codex_arithmetic
title: A rational chart for four regular quintuples with explicit square-root lifting
